newsitem.title: GERMANY: Global vegetable oil stocks seen declining.
newsitem.headline: Global vegetable oil stocks seen declining.

text.p: World stocks of oils and fats are seen falling throughout March, followed by a slight decline over the year-earlier period in April/September, the Oil World newsletter said.
Soy oil stocks were put at 2.31 million tonnes by the end of March 1997 compared with 2.70 million at the end of November 1996 and 2.58 million at end-March 1996.
The stocks forecast for sun oil at end-March was 1.24 million (1.19 and 1.32 respectively at the two earlier dates), rape oil 1.10 million (1.41 and 1.21) and palm oil 2.04 million (3.13 and 2.23).
Oil World said palm oil stocks would recover in April/September 1997 but this would not be enough to offset further cuts in sunflower, rape, cotton and groundnut oils.
Rotterdam vegetable oil stocks declined sharply in February and early March stocks of 207.2 million tonnes were down from 279.4 million a month earlier, Oil World also noted.
Rotterdam warehouse stocks of 14 products were 341.3 million in early October 1996 and 296.4 million in March 1996.
Oil World cited a lower European rapeseed crush from the reduced 1996 domestic crop, a lower U.S. oil content and buoyant Chinese oil import demand.
